section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single study that adapted the CEMS and IES-2 into Brazilian Portuguese and evaluated their psychometric properties in Brazilian adults. The authors report model modifications to attain adequate fit, measurement invariance across sex for the scales, and significant (but non-reported) correlations between restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages (RCM), body valorisation (BV), and BMI for both women and men; several scale items were eliminated and BMI was calculated from self-reported height and weight.

section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion reports translation and adaptation of the CEMS and IES-2 into Brazilian Portuguese and psychometric evaluation in Brazilian adults, noting some item eliminations and correlated error terms to achieve adequate model fit and measurement invariance across sex. The authors describe significant relationships among caregiver eating messages, intuitive eating factors, body appreciation (BAS), and BMI but do not present numeric sample size or Pearson correlation coefficients in this section. Limitations include non-probabilistic recruitment, predominance of Caucasians, mostly well-educated participants, and use of self-reported height and weight.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single study (Study X) that translated and adapted the CEMS and IES-2 into Brazilian Portuguese and evaluated their psychometric properties in Brazilian adults, finding acceptable factorial validity after minor item eliminations and correlated constructs. The models showed invariance across sex, and nomological analyses indicated negative correlations between restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages and body appreciation, as well as weak negative associations between body appreciation subscales and BMI for both women and men.
section_summary.evidence_source: This study translated and adapted the CEMS and IES-2 into  Brazilian Portuguese and examined their psychometric properties in samples of Brazilian Portuguese-speaking adults. We also found a significant negative correlation between RCM scores and BV scores, in both women and men. BMI correlated with RCM, BV, BC and RHCS for males and RCM, RHSC, BFCC, BV and BC factors for women.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion reports the translation and psychometric evaluation of the CEMS and IES-2 for Brazilian Portuguese-speaking adults, noting model modifications were required but theoretical structure retained and models showed (at least) invariance across sex. The authors report associations between restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages (RCM) and lower body appreciation (BV) and correlations between RCM, BMI and several BAS/IES-2 factors for both sexes, and they note limitations including non-probabilistic sampling, predominance of Caucasians, mostly well-educated participants, and use of self-reported height and weight.
